body.statement: Let \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}=(M,E_{\mathrm{obs}})\) be a finite undirected graph with all diagonal positions specified.  Call \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) completable when every real symmetric partial matrix whose principal submatrix on every clique is positive definite admits a positive-definite completion.  Then \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is completable if and only if it is chordal.  Consequently, if \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\) is chordal, \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})\) admits a positive-definite completion if and only if \(\mathcal Q_{\pi,j}(G_{\mathrm{obs}})[C,C]\succ0\) for every maximal clique \(C\) of \(G_{\mathrm{obs}}\); a completion can be produced by the sequential filling process for chordal partial matrices.

source.locator: Definition of partial positive and completable graphs in Section 5, Theorem 7 on page 120, and the sequential completion process in Section 7 on pages 122--123
source.verbatim_statement: \(\text{THEOREM 7. }G\text{ is completable if and only if }G\text{ is chordal.}\)

attestation.note: Transcribed from Theorem 7 of the source-of-record PDF; the maximal-clique formulation unfolds the paper's definition of a partial positive matrix, and the constructive clause is located in its Section 7 completion process.

body.justification: This is the classical graph-theoretic existence criterion needed to turn coordinatewise partial disturbance covariances into full positive-definite certificates on chordal observation graphs.
body.gap: GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the matrix-completion substrate; it does not derive the LiMVAM residual criterion, coefficient uniqueness, or the four-cycle observed-moment obstruction proved here.
body.consumer: The chordal branch of \(\text{thm:calibration-graph-completion}\) invokes this result after reducing LiMVAM feasibility to one partial covariance matrix per variable.
